notes: Third sweep (2026-10-22-b, head 0397dec): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. reads is empty in all five and no transcript has a Read or Skill call on a skill file (the only Skill hit is the tool definition); the tool calls are Write, Edit and Bash, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. In the scratch folder all five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors and pass mix format --check-formatted (Elixir 1.20.4). Doctests: only opus-1 has examples, 2 pass.

Changed rule since db91c23: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function" gained "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; ...). Graded against the current text, it changes no verdict here: opus-1 line 40 (fetch_currency/2, a public def in a @moduledoc false module) is the one run it covers, and the unchanged "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." already decides it; haiku-1 line 82 (public parse/1) is decided by "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step", since its body calls build/4; haiku-1 line 170 and sonnet-1 line 139 are private one-step withs decided by the first sentence. Violating runs out of 5: one-step with 3 (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1); else 0; case nested in a with body 0. Sonnet-2's parse/1 is a case on Map.fetch whose {:ok, atom} branch calls build/2, which can fail; the rule's second-step sentence speaks of the body of a one-step with, so it is not counted. The other changes since db91c23 (the do: rule, the captures rule, Assert with patterns) are outside this case's list, and no run breaks the do: rule.

Naming, violating runs out of 5 per sentence: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean ? 0 (not exercised); get/fetch 3 (opus-1 six fetch_* helpers, haiku-1 four, sonnet-1 three, all looking a key up and checking the value); size/length 0; ignored values 0; domain variable names 2 (sonnet-1 dt line 146; sonnet-2 dt line 109, n line 117, c line 122), held to the 2026-10-21 standard that flagged dt and single letters; ts, atom, kind, body, fields, entry, parsed_data and type_string are not counted. data from the "data" key is allowed in every run.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweeps' standard. Missing fields reported as invalid through a _ -> after Map.get (haiku-2) are counted under Read required keys and Match every expected shape; after Map.fetch (haiku-1) only under Match every expected shape, since Map.fetch is not the nil-returning access the required-keys rule names. haiku-1's and haiku-2's catch-all parse/1 returning :invalid_payload or :malformed_envelope for any missing top-level key goes in checks only, as before. sonnet-1 line 69 and sonnet-2 line 71 (nil -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "data"}} after Enum.find over the keys) give the right answer in the probe but infer the field from which head matched, so they count under the struct rule, as 2026-10-21 counted baseline-sonnet-2 line 78. sonnet-1's optional_string/2 _ -> nil counts under Match every expected shape, as 2026-10-21 counted baseline-sonnet-2's _ -> {:ok, nil}. A parse/1 head that binds keys only its guard uses (haiku-1, haiku-2) is clean; keys bound and used only in the body (sonnet-1 id, type, created; sonnet-2 type) are violations, as before. A public parse/1 without @doc (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2) counts under Comments; a @doc without ## Examples (sonnet-1) is clean. An if inside a with and a case inside a case go under Keep functions short in other_violations.

Borderline Comments call: opus-1 lines 3-4 ("# Validating accessors for string-keyed payload maps. Errors carry the key as given, so callers can report exactly which field was wrong.") sit under @moduledoc false in an internal module and their second sentence gives a reason, so they are not counted, as the previous sweep did not count opus-1's reason comment at lines 184-185; counted, Opus would be violated on Comments. The public functions of the @moduledoc false Fields module without @doc are not counted.

Probe of 23 payloads in the scratch folder: every run returns an unsupported-type error for "invoice.paid" and reports a known type without amount as a field error, not as unsupported. opus-1 names every missing and invalid field correctly. haiku-1 and haiku-2 report every missing data field as {:invalid_field, key} and any missing or ill-typed top-level key as :invalid_payload / :malformed_envelope. sonnet-1 names every field correctly but accepts "customer_email" => 5 as nil. sonnet-2 names every field correctly but reports "type" => 123 as {:unsupported_type, 123}.

Compared with the 2026-10-22 baseline: Opus moves from clean to violated on the with rule (one-step with) and on Naming (fetch_* helpers), and from violated to clean on Comments; Opus stays violated on Read required keys and clean on Match every expected shape. Haiku stays violated on Read required keys, Match every expected shape, the with rule, Naming and Comments. Sonnet moves from clean to violated on Read required keys (sonnet-2's payload["created"]) and on the multi-clause rule (type bound in the head in both runs), and stays violated on Match every expected shape, the with rule, the struct rule, Naming and Comments. Atoms and the return-tuple rule stay clean in every tier.
